narrative:
The 2023 San Francisco Giants entered the season with measured optimism — a roster built on depth rather than stars, hoping Logan Webb could anchor a competitive club in a wide-open NL West. The early going was rocky, a 11-15 April marked by bullpen blunders and crushing home runs allowed, including a devastating three-run shot by Nick Maton off Camilo Doval that epitomized the closer's inconsistency. Yet the Giants were never far from moments of genuine electricity, like Blake Sabol's go-ahead blast that briefly made Oracle Park believe in something special.

May and June represented the season's true heartbeat. The Giants surged to a 17-12 May and then an extraordinary 18-8 June — the best stretch of baseball the club would play all year. Veterans like Brandon Crawford delivered in the clutch, rookie Patrick Bailey announced himself with timely home runs, and the offense strung together enough rallies to make the Giants feel like genuine playoff contenders. For a few weeks in midsummer, San Francisco sat within striking distance of a Wild Card spot, and the June run felt like a foundation being laid for something lasting.

July and August told a more complicated story. The Giants went 13-13 in July — competent but not decisive — before sliding to 12-15 in August as the bullpen continued to betray them. Tyler Rogers and Camilo Doval surrendered critical home runs at the worst possible moments, and a Bryce Harper three-run shot in late August delivered a particularly demoralizing blow during what should have been a stretch run push. Patrick Bailey's heroics — including an 0.852 WPA home run in August — provided the lone bright spots, but the losses were piling up in ways the wins could not fully offset.

September rendered its verdict swiftly and harshly. A 9-18 collapse in the final month of the season extinguished any remaining playoff hopes and pushed the Giants to a losing 79-83 record. Doval's late-game collapses became a painful recurring theme, and a disputed home-plate collision single in mid-September symbolized a team undone by the smallest margins. Michael Conforto's late game-winning single on September 25th was a bittersweet footnote — a flash of what might have been on a team that spent the season oscillating between genuinely good and deeply frustrating, ultimately falling short of the October baseball their June form had once seemed to promise.

chapters.title: Rocky Launch
chapters.description: A turbulent April saw the Giants stumble out of the gate, with bullpen meltdowns and costly home runs defining an 11-15 month.

chapters.title: The Giants Catch Fire
chapters.description: A 17-12 May accelerated into an 18-8 June as San Francisco played its best baseball of the year, with Bailey, Crawford, and Yastrzemski all delivering in big moments.

chapters.title: Treading Water
chapters.description: A 13-13 July kept the Giants in the conversation but revealed a team unable to string together the decisive wins needed to separate themselves from the Wild Card pack.

chapters.title: Slipping Away
chapters.description: A 12-15 August featured Patrick Bailey heroics alongside damaging bullpen implosions, as the Giants' playoff window began closing faster than they could stop it.

chapters.title: September Collapse
chapters.description: A brutal 9-18 September buried the Giants for good, with Camilo Doval's late-game failures and a crushing run differential sealing a disappointing 79-83 finish.
